flags.text: For some reason, my PC and my laptop, keep popping up that different games Have a cloud sync error on steam. I imagine it’s because the saved data and begin and everything is saved onto my external hard drive, which I unplugged and plug back in all the time. flags.note: You don't need to re-add the library: Connect Steam adds the drive to Steam once per computer and Steam remembers it, so the games just show as not installed while the drive is out. Cloud saves for most games live on C: (Steam's own folder or Documents), not on the drive. The errors most likely come from unplugging or shutting down before Steam finishes uploading a save, then playing on the other computer. Before you unplug, wait a few seconds after quitting a game until the Library shows the game's cloud status as up to date; if a conflict pops up, pick the side with the newer save.

proposals.title: Labyrinth trial rooms in the Tower
proposals.summary: Reworked: the Labyrinth now flashes and goes pitch black, your light stops at walls so you have to feel your way through dead ends, only the riddle gate locks glow (plus the odd pair of eyes), and a key in one dead end lights dim torches across the whole room. Floors you're already partway through stay exactly the same.
proposals.feedback: This is actually such a cool idea! Don’t resolve my flag about unique challenge rooms for the game mode because I want more ideas like this, but absolutely let’s integrate this. I like the labyrinth idea at Alexis core, however, I would love for you to apply somewhat differently. Make the whole room. Go pitch black after a flash of light When you enter. The only things visible is directly around you similar to the existing dark rooms, and glowing ruins on the Riddle Gates. Everything else is literally invisible except maybe occasional ambience, glowing or torches or maybe even fun, monster animations or something. The light that the player exudes though only shines on the walls around them, meaning you can see up and down in a vertical hallway, but not very far, and can’t see past the walls on either side. That way you can’t just work the maze out in your head, but actually have to try different pathways, hit dead ends, and etc. maybe make a key in one deadend allow you to turn on torches that dimly light the whole room so once you solve it you can come back without having to resolve it. Make sense?
